title: Blocking IO on ForkJoinPool.commonPool(): resource starvation, isolation problem
shortTitle: Why is blocking IO on commonPool dangerous?
keyPoints: ForkJoinPool.commonPool() is JVM-wide, shared, and has only cores - 1 threads designed for short CPU-bound tasks.
Blocking IO on commonPool threads exhausts the pool, starving parallelStream, other CFs, and framework async operations.
One slow dependency (2-second DB query) on 3 threads can stall the entire application.
This is a resource isolation failure: one component's blocking IO affects unrelated components.
Fix: dedicated ExecutorService per concern with named threads, bounded queues, and monitoring.
Leave commonPool free for parallelStream and lightweight CPU-bound tasks.

s1_definition.oneliner: Blocking IO on ForkJoinPool.commonPool() exhausts its few shared threads, starving all other CompletableFutures, parallel streams, and frameworks that share the pool, causing a resource isolation failure.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **commonPool** – JVM-wide shared pool with `cores - 1` threads, designed for short CPU-bound work.
- **Shared users** – `CompletableFuture.supplyAsync()`, `parallelStream()`, `Arrays.parallelSort()`, and many frameworks all use the same pool.
- **Resource starvation** – blocking IO (JDBC, HTTP) on commonPool threads prevents any other work from executing.
- **Isolation failure** – one component's slow dependency cascades to unrelated components sharing the pool.
- **Fix** – dedicated `ExecutorService` per concern: IO pool (many threads), CPU pool (cores), commonPool left free.
s1_definition.analogy: The commonPool is National Bank of India's only conference room with 3 seats. Department A books it for a 2-hour meeting (blocking JDBC). Department B needs a 5-minute standup: wait 2 hours. Department C needs to review reports: wait. One slow department blocks everyone because they share the same room. Dedicated pools give each department their own room.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  commonPool (3 threads, shared)
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Thread-1: JDBC query (2s BLOCKED)       │
  │ Thread-2: JDBC query (2s BLOCKED)       │
  │ Thread-3: JDBC query (2s BLOCKED)       │
  │                                          │
  │ parallelStream: QUEUED (no threads!)     │
  │ supplyAsync:    QUEUED (no threads!)     │
  │ framework:      QUEUED (no threads!)     │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────┘
  Everything stalls for 2 seconds!
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Running blocking IO on ForkJoinPool.commonPool() is a resource isolation failure. The pool has only cores - 1 threads and is shared by all CompletableFutures, parallel streams, and many frameworks. Blocking all threads with database queries or HTTP calls starves everything in the JVM. One slow dependency cascades to affect the entire application.

The fix is dedicated executors per concern. IO pool with many threads for blocking calls. CPU pool with cores threads for computation. CommonPool left free for parallel streams and lightweight tasks. Named threads for debugging. Bounded queues for back-pressure.

At National Bank of India, dashboard widgets making JDBC calls blocked commonPool, stalling the reporting parallel streams. Customers waited 2 extra seconds for reports. Moving JDBC to a dedicated IO pool eliminated the cross-contamination.

Remember one sentence: blocking IO on commonPool starves everything; use dedicated pools per concern.
